paragraphs: In the morning, review record coding. In the afternoon, investigate changes and denials. At quarter-end, complete statistics. Work is indoors and system-based, driven by settlement and quality-control deadlines with significant responsibility.

In short, they turn healthcare into reliable data. They enter information, assign codes, correct errors, support insurance, and ensure quarter-end statistics, combining system work with accountability.

According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), about 194,800 Medical Records Specialists were employed in 2024. Employment is projected to rise to 208,600 by 2034, a net increase of about 13,800 jobs, with around 14,200 openings annually and a 2026 median annual wage of about $50,300 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace Medical Records Specialists, but it will take over automatic coding. Extraction and initial coding automate routine records, shifting specialists from template entry toward complex-record judgment, coding review, and compliance. Template-only workers face pressure, while reviewers remain stable.
